title: Empowering Local Communities Through Education
author: Aaron
body:
Creating opportunities for young people to grow and prosper is a key component of the change the APT Foundation is striving to bring about in the world.

With the APT Travel Group (ATG) having a long history in Western Australia’s Kimberley region, we are mindful of many of the issues faced by Aboriginal people there. The Kimberley is known to have one of the highest rates of suicide in the world, with the region’s young people being particularly vulnerable.

Education is the most important means by which to empower and create resilient children. The APT Foundation is making a noticeable difference in the Kimberley, having recently contributed $14,000 to the Kandiwal Community. This donation has made the possibility of hiring a part-time teacher a reality. While the School of the Air remains the main source of education for the children, being equipped to offer students face-to-face learning is an important step in providing a more positive future.

As the APT Foundation’s Madeleine Curtain says: ‘Equitable and quality education is an important sustainability goal of the United Nations and is a key focus of the APT Foundation’s community work around the world’. Increasing the access to education, while ensuring that learning keeps pace with technology, is fundamental to improving the wellbeing of individuals and communities.

Located in a highly remote part of the Kimberley, the Kandiwal community are members of the Wunambal people, who welcome visitors to Ngauwudu (Mitchell Plateau). It is here that APT’s Mitchell Falls Wilderness Lodge provides a touch of luxury in the wilderness for its guests.

Building upon the relationships APT has developed with local Indigenous communities, through its Kimberley Wilderness Adventures, the APT Foundation will continue to roll out a range of initiatives in support of the Kimberley and its people.
